grades.quote: The atomic exchange instructions on the two processors will both be writing into the cache block containing the spinlock.
grades.reason: Directly says that with a basic atomic-exchange spinlock, waiting processors all write into the same cache block. It contrasts this with cache-conscious spinlocks, which wait using only reads to avoid coherence traffic.

grades.quote: If the two processors keep alternately writing into the same block, there will be continual traffic on the memory interconnect as the cache block is transferred back and forth between the two caches.
grades.reason: Describes the basic exchange-based spinlock, which repeatedly swaps while waiting. It also explains the coherence mechanism: a write invalidates other caches' copies, and alternating writers cause continual interconnect traffic. It does not explicitly tie this to contended lock waiting, which the neighboring passage does.

grades.quote: Each iteration swaps one into lk->locked and checks the previous value; if the previous value is zero, then we’ve acquired the lock
grades.reason: Describes an amoswap-based spinlock on RISC-V, where each loop iteration performs an atomic swap. It says nothing about cache-coherence traffic or contention cost, so it only gives background on the lock.
Introduces the Zacas compare-and-swap extension. It does not cover atomic-exchange spinlocks or the cache-coherence traffic they generate under contention.
